messages.subject: Re: Stan and Math v2.7.1
parts:
On Monday, August 31, 2015 at 3:44:57 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Here's where I think we stand:

Math:
- code complete (yes, we're missing Krzysztof's tests, but I think we can tag now)
- tag v2.7.1 today (Daniel)

Stan:
- code remaining:
  * sparse multiply (Krzysztof)
  * anything else? If we want this out asap, we should bump advi-adapt-eta.
- tag v2.7.1 when we say we need it (Daniel)

Ben, can you confirm everything above? No one else is pushing for v2.7.1, so when you say it's ready, we can tag.

I need to do a PR for Stan to doc inv_Phi. I would say that ADVI in its current form is not really widely usable, so if we bump advi-adapt-eta, then we need to unexpose vb() in rstan and eliminate the option to call vb() from rstanarm. That is a pretty big price to pay, so if Dustin / Alp think it is feasible to merge advi-adapt-eta in the next couple of days, then it is worth waiting for.

Ben

Hi!

As far as I understood, you plan to advertise with 2.7.1 the autodiff library, so maybe this is of interest in this context: Currently the issue

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/133

is still open. It describes test failures of g++ 4.4.7 & Intel compilers in stan-math. The g++ 4.4.7 is part of RedHat Linux Enterprise 6.5 which is installed in many production systems.

Moreover: Are those tests which fail critical? Can I not trust stan if those tests above fail with my compiler? Is there somewhere some information where users can get such information (how severe a failing stan-math test is with their compiler)?

Best,
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan and Math v2.7.1
parts:
They may just be overly sensitive tests that are tripped up by
MKL's non-compliant arithmetic like the other bugs we've tracked
down.

But even were we to relax the constraints in the tests,
users will have to decide for themselves how much the Intel
compiler's lowered arithmetic precision is worth in terms of
speed or accuracy --- we don't know the answer ourselves.

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan and Math v2.7.1
parts:
Hi Bob!

The MKL+Intel is more sensitive than other configurations, yes. But note that I reported also results for Intel without MKL and for the g++ 4.4.7 without the MKL. So there are issues which affect RHEL6.5 installations which use g++ 4.4.7 as it was reported in the issue.

BTW, I have disabled MKL in all tests here run with stan-math.

Sebastian
